subject: Urgent: Lumenex real-time session stalls during high concurrency — exec sync & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumenex.com>

Cc: Eli Turner <eli.turner@lumenex.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T08:12:34-07:00
Subject: Realtime sessions stalling — demo failing (request id: 3f9a-req1234)

Priya —

We hit repeated stalls in our production demo environment this morning between 07:45–08:05 PDT. Clients report the client app receives initial tokens, then the socket appears to hang for 6–12s and eventually times out with a 504/WS close. We captured client-side logs and a sample request id (3f9a-req1234). Attached is lumenex_initial_logs.txt with the full capture.

Impact: our internal demo to an enterprise prospect was interrupted and the residue caused a rollback on the demo flow. This is high-impact — we’re flagged as a P1 on our side. We need an ETA and mitigation steps we can apply immediately (either a quick config change or routing).

Key details from our side:
- Concurrent sessions during the incident ~ 420 (bursting from 90 to 420)
- Predominantly Chat streaming (chunked transfer / websocket)
- We saw repeated chunk gaps and occasional 502s from the Redwood edge

Please advise next steps; we’re standing by for a live call.

— Samira
SRE, Lumenex

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <samira.khan@lumenex.com>, Eli Turner <eli.turner@lumenex.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T10:30:22-07:00
Subject: Initial triage: observed chunk gaps + proxy backpressure (req window 07:40–08:10 PDT)

Summary of what I’m seeing from our telemetry for the request window you provided:
- Edge proxy (proxy-rt1) spiked 502s and saw a transient backlog on socket write buffers when concurrency > 300.
- Token emission telemetry shows the model did stream initial tokens then stalled — no clear model-level OOMs. KV cache hit rates were normal.
- Chunk coalescing component had a sharp increase in coalescing latency for small fragments (~10–40ms -> 200–600ms) which aligns with the 6–12s user-observed stall when compounded across multiple bursts.

Hypothesis: a combination of proxy backpressure + our chunk coalescing threshold behavior under high concurrency created serialized flush delays. This shows up as long gaps between emitted frames rather than a continuous stream.

Immediate mitigations to try (recommend order):
A) Re-route Lumenex traffic to a dedicated serving pool (controls isolation and reduces noisy neighbor backpressure). This requires a config flip on routing (can be done in ~5–10m) and will cost a small transient uplift.
B) Temporarily lower the chunk coalescing threshold to force earlier flushes for small fragments (risk: slightly higher token overhead).
C) Increase idle websocket keepalive frequency at the edge (short-term will surface stuck sockets faster and avoid client timeouts).

I’ve pulled trace-logs-req1234.txt (attached) and started an internal perf capture on the proxy nodes. If Marissa can confirm the traffic source (hosted vs dedicated) I’ll push the routing flip.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
